MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section I: Presidential Vetoes
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
According to Article 77 & 82, the President may veto a bill by returning it to the Assembly with a written statement. The articles do not contain any information on how to override a veto. As a consequence, the President has an “absolute” veto power that cannot even be overriden with a supermajority in the Grand Assembly of Sordland.

We may introduce a limit to vetoes by giving the Grand National Assembly the right to override a veto with a supermajority. If we prefer, we can also establish a loophole by not introducing a time limit for the president to act on a bill, giving them an absolute pocket veto power.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section II: Constitutional Amendment Process
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle: According to Article 5 of the Constitution, an amendment that has the support of at least 150 signatures may be proposed to the Grand National Assembly. A two-thirds majority vote in the Grand National Assembly and a simple majority vote in the Supreme Court is required for the amendment. As a consequence, the Supreme Court, which is not part of the elected legislative branch, has voting rights that give them enormous power in the amendment process.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section III: Impeachment of the President
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
According to Article 17, the President of Sordland is not responsible for the actions performed in the exercise of presidential duties, except in the case of high treason or violation of the Constitution. In such cases, the President may be impeached by the Supreme Court in joint session, with an absolute majority of its members. 

Therefore, the impeachment process only includes the Supreme Court and it gives them great power over the executive.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section IV: Appointment of Ministers
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
According to the Constitution, the President appoints the ministers to the Council of Ministers from elected members of the Assembly.

We may introduce a confidence vote by adding the line: "The President may nominate ministers which will require a confidence vote from the Grand National Assembly for their appointment," or include the Assembly more in the process with: "The Grand National Assembly may nominate a list of ministers, which the President may appoint."

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section V: Electoral Threshold
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
According to Article 50, a political party needs a minimum of 10% of the total national vote to win seats in the Grand National Assembly. The votes of the parties who pass the threshold are re-distributed proportionally, meaning USP, which currently holds the lead, would be the main beneficiary.

Decreasing the threshold may allow the Workers Party of Bludia and the Communist Party of Sordland to be elected in the next elections. Increasing the threshold, however, may put the National Front Party below the threshold.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section VI: Presidential Decrees
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
According to Article 18 and 51, the President is able to issue decrees on political, social, and economic issues that would carry the force of law: they could not contradict the constitution and are subject to judicial review. Therefore, the President may issue decrees in many subjects without going through the Grand National Assembly. However, the Assembly may pass legislation on the same subjects to override presidential decrees. 

We may include the Assembly in the process by requiring an enabling act from the Assembly to be able to enact decrees, or we may strengthen them by making them have priority over statute law and not subject to judicial review.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section VII: Term Limits
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle: According to the Constitution, the President shall be elected to serve for four years. However, there is no mention of a term limit, allowing one individual to be able to run, be elected and serve as President without limits.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section VIII: Immunity of Justices
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
The Constitution gives the Justices of the Supreme Court absolute immunity before the law and describes no procedure of impeachment, making them untouchable by the other branches of government.

We may describe an impeachment procedure by giving the Grand National Assembly the right to propose an impeachment of a Justice on the legal grounds of unconstitutional behaviour, or we may give the President complete control over the Court by giving them the right to replace Justices.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Section IX: "Member of Honor" Rights of Tarquin Soll
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle:
Article 99 of the Constitution defines the "Member of Honor" title, and the rights their members may exercise. A Member of Honor has absolute immunity and is considered to be a permanent member of the Grand National Assembly. They are given control of their own personal security team, provided by the state’s Presidential Guards. A member is also eligible to live in a special private residence provided by the State for free. 

The only person who holds the title is Tarquin Soll.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Economic Strategy
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle: A focus on strengthening our resource economy involves leveraging natural assets and safeguarding long-term energy commitments. Alternatively, diversifying the economy beyond resource reliance aims for a balanced financial landscape, mitigating over-reliance risks. A mixed strategy offers more flexibility.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Foreign Affairs Strategy
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle: The Kingdom faces new diplomatic choices. Interventionism encourages active military involvement, while Appeasement aims to strengthen ties with Wehlen and Rumburg's monarchy. Alternatively, you could choose the Third Way, forming regional alliances with Derdia, Pales, and Morella to avoid major powers.

MultipleChoicePageProperties.Title: Government Structure Intention
MultipleChoicePageProperties.Subtitle: Opting for Absolutism would solidify monarchic traditions within House Toras, while considering Reform aligns with House Sazon and the Rizian People's Party, signaling a shift towards wider civic participation and resource redistribution. Conversely, the Status Quo upholds the current balance of power and provincial autonomy.
